steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Ferrous metals contain iron - magnetic, prone to rust (except stainless). Mild steel: low carbon, ductile, weldable. Stainless steel: chromium content prevents corrosion - cutlery, medical instruments.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Cast iron: high carbon (2-4%), excellent compressive strength, self-lubricating - engine blocks, manhole covers.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Aluminium: lightweight (1/3 steel's density), corrosion-resistant (oxide layer), excellent conductor - aircraft, cans, window frames.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Copper: excellent electrical and thermal conductor, ductile, malleable, antimicrobial - wiring, plumbing, PCBs.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain why stainless steel is used for surgical instruments whereas mild steel is not, despite both being ferrous metals. | Justify the use of aluminium rather than steel for aircraft fuselage construction. | A product designer needs a gold-coloured, corrosion-resistant material for a door handle. Compare brass and gold-anodised aluminium.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Stainless steel has 10.5%+ chromium which forms a passive chromium oxide layer - self-healing, prevents rust even when scratched. Mild steel has no chromium and rusts rapidly. | Aluminium: density 2.7 g/cm3 vs steel 7.8 - 1/3 the weight, crucial for fuel efficiency; corrosion-resistant; good strength-to-weight when alloyed. Trade-off: more expensive and less stiff. | Brass: genuine gold appearance, naturally corrosion-resistant, heavy and tactile (premium feel), low friction, antimicrobial. steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Ferrous = contains iron (think ferrum = Latin for iron) Know that stainless steel is ferrous but does not rust - explain WHY (chromium oxide layer) State alloy composition: brass = copper + zinc, bronze = copper + tin
